questions.stem: What is the key difference between a scalar and a vector quantity?

options.text: Vectors can only be positive, while scalars can be negative
Vectors have both magnitude and direction, while scalars have magnitude only
Scalars are always larger than vectors
Scalars have units but vectors do not

questions.explanation: A vector quantity has both magnitude (size) and direction, while a scalar quantity has magnitude only.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector because it has both magnitude and direction. Speed, mass, and energy are all scalar quantities.

questions.stem: Two forces of 5 N and 3 N act on an object in the same direction. What is the resultant force?
questions.explanation: When vectors act in the same direction, their magnitudes are added: 5 N + 3 N = 8 N.

questions.stem: A person walks 3 km east, then 4 km north. What is the magnitude of their resultant displacement?
questions.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, use Pythagoras' theorem: R = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5 km.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly shows a scalar and its related vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed (scalar) and velocity (vector) are a classic scalar-vector pair. Speed tells you how fast; velocity tells you how fast and in which direction.

questions.stem: When representing a vector as an arrow, what does the length of the arrow indicate?
questions.explanation: When vectors are drawn as arrows, the length represents the magnitude (size) and the arrow's direction shows the direction of the vector.

questions.stem: A car travels at 30 m/s around a circular bend at constant speed. What can be said about its velocity?

options.text: Its velocity is 30 m/s in all directions
Its velocity is changing because its direction is changing
Its velocity is constant because its speed is constant
Its velocity is zero because it travels in a circle

questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so it depends on both speed and direction. Even though the speed is constant, the direction is changing, so the velocity is changing.
